summary.text: The Giza pyramid complex in Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid, the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure, their associated complexes and the Great Sphinx.
All were built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom, between about 2600 and 2500 BC.
The site also includes temples, cemeteries and the remains of a workers' village, at the edge of the Western Desert near Cairo.

facts.label: Great Pyramid built
facts.value: Also called Khufu's pyramid; c. 2580 to c. 2560 BC

facts.label: Distance from Cairo
facts.value: About 13 km southwest of the city centre

facts.label: Seven Wonders status
facts.value: Oldest Wonder and the only one still standing

items.prompt: Standing at Giza, one pyramid looks bigger than its neighbour built for Khufu. Why is that look misleading?

options.label: It stands on higher ground and is steeper
It is made of much larger limestone blocks
It has far more casing stone covering it
It was built much later and so is taller

items.explain: Khafre's pyramid sits higher and rises at a steeper angle, but it is in fact smaller in both height and volume.

items.prompt: Of the ancient world's Seven Wonders, only one can still be visited. Which?
items.explain: The Great Pyramid was listed as a Wonder and is the oldest of them and the only one still in existence.

items.prompt: Egyptologists broadly agree on whose face the Great Sphinx carries. Whose?

options.label: Khufu, whose pyramid is the Great Pyramid
Menkaure, whose pyramid is the smallest
Antipater, who listed the Seven Wonders
Khafre, whose pyramid sits near the Sphinx

items.explain: The consensus is that the Sphinx's head is Khafre's, and a Sphinx temple is part of Khafre's complex.

items.prompt: Builders at Giza needed vast amounts of limestone. Where did most of it come from?

options.label: Quarries at Tura, across the river
The rock formation under the site itself

items.explain: Most of the limestone originates from the underlying Mokattam Formation; the fine white casing stones came from Tura.

items.prompt: Three pits were cut beside the Great Pyramid. What did the two on its south side hold when they were excavated?
items.explain: The boat pits contained a ship, and the two on the south side held intact ships when excavated.

items.prompt: Khufu's pyramid once had a smooth outer layer, and a few pieces remain at its base. What were those casing stones made of?

options.label: Dark basalt from the temple floors

items.explain: The remaining casing stones were fine white limestone quarried at Tura.
